solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Scotsman’s side upset supporter

indicators.note: in a down-to-earth sense upset means turned over, so the word for side is read the other way round

blocks.note: Jock is a familiar name for a Scotsman
a side in a dispute is one of its parts

explanation.surface: A Scotsman's football team loses and a fan is upset.
explanation.walkthrough: Jock is the stock nickname for a Scot; 'supporter' pretends to be a football fan but is the garment.
explanation.definitionFit: An athletic support worn by sportsmen is literally a protective supporter garment.

clue.text: Almost a month engaged in setting up military government

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the month's name loses its final letter
in a down clue setting something up raises it, so the short word for engaged in is read bottom to top

blocks.note: the sixth month
to be at something is to be engaged in it

explanation.surface: A month spent plotting a coup to install army rule.
explanation.walkthrough: JUNE without its last letter, then AT reversed: JUN + TA.
explanation.definitionFit: A junta is a group of officers ruling a country after seizing power by force.

clue.text: Against taking sieve by force

blocks.note: con is the argument against, as in pros and cons
to strain liquid is to pass it through a sieve

explanation.surface: Someone objects to a sieve being used by force.
explanation.definitionFit: To constrain someone is to compel or oblige them, which is what forcing them means.

clue.text: Cleaner getting work over time on sets primarily of shows like Corrie

indicators.note: primarily means in the first place, so only the opening letter of sets is kept

blocks.note: soap is a cleaning agent
op is short for opus, a work
an era is a period of time
first letter of sets

explanation.surface: A cleaner works overtime on the sets of a TV studio.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'work over time' puts OP above ERA. Corrie is Coronation Street, a long-running British TV serial set in a Manchester street.
explanation.definitionFit: Coronation Street is the classic example of a long-running domestic drama serial on television.

clue.text: Fellow on Ecstasy thrown out of dining room in clergyman’s residence

indicators.note: things thrown out of a room are no longer inside it, so those letters are removed from the room's name

blocks.note: F is the abbreviation for fellow
E is slang for the drug ecstasy
a refectory is a communal dining hall, as in a college or monastery

explanation.surface: A college fellow high on drugs is ejected from the dining hall at the vicarage.
explanation.walkthrough: Take F and E out of REFECTORY to leave RECTORY.
explanation.definitionFit: A rectory is the house provided for a rector, a parish priest, to live in.

clue.text: Penny finding the last part not yet finished

blocks.note: p is the abbreviation for a penny
the ending is the last part of something

explanation.surface: Penny finds the final chapter still to be written.
explanation.definitionFit: A pending matter is one still awaiting decision or completion, unresolved for now.

clue.text: Support for international singer overwhelming

indicators.note: to overwhelm is to engulf completely, so one piece surrounds the other

blocks.note: a bass is a singer with the lowest male voice
I is the abbreviation for international

explanation.surface: A singer dominates the world stage with backing for an international star.
explanation.definitionFit: A basis is the foundation that something rests on, the underlying support for it.

clue.text: King after an expression of dissatisfaction shows reserve

blocks.note: a boo is a jeer of disapproval
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A king is booed and keeps his distance.
explanation.definitionFit: To book a table or seat is to reserve it in advance, the verb sense.

clue.text: Country songs about embracing end of journey

indicators.note: about can mean turned around, so the word for songs is read backwards
the end of a word is its final letter, so only that one is kept
to embrace is to hold in the arms, so one piece wraps around the other

blocks.note: airs are tunes or songs
last letter of journey

explanation.surface: Country and western songs about the end of a long trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Country songs' reads as a genre, but Country alone is the definition. AIRS reversed is SRIA, which holds Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Syria is a nation in the Middle East, so it is one example of a country.

clue.text: Music producer’s staying power seen at Dutch bar earlier

blocks.note: steel is toughness of character, the resolve to keep going
to bar something is to ban it
D is the abbreviation for Dutch

explanation.surface: A record producer shows stamina in an Amsterdam bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'earlier' puts the bar word before the Dutch letter. The 's is read as 'is': the music producer is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A steel band is a Caribbean ensemble playing pans, so it makes music and can be called a producer of it.

clue.text: Grandma of northern girl whichever way you look at it

indicators.text: whichever way you look at it
indicators.note: reading from either side gives the same thing, so the result is identical forwards and backwards

blocks.note: N is the abbreviation for northern
Anna is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A grandmother from the north of England seen from every angle.
explanation.definitionFit: Nanna is an affectionate family name for a grandmother, used by her grandchildren.

clue.text: Coming together to utter obscenities over working at company

indicators.note: one piece goes over, covering, the others, so it surrounds them

blocks.note: to curse is to swear
a machine that is on is working
Co is the abbreviation for company

explanation.surface: Swearing on the job at the office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at company' simply places the company abbreviation after the working word, and the swearing word wraps both.
explanation.definitionFit: A concourse is a gathering or flocking together of people or things, a formal word for a meeting.

clue.text: Immense novel so romantic

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters are made into something new

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A huge, sweeping romance novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like a noun, a book, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Astronomic figures are vast, like the distances studied in astronomy, so the word means enormous.

clue.text: Dance in clogs endlessly

indicators.note: without an end means the final letter is cut off

blocks.note: to clump and block, as snow does on a boot sole, so clogs here is a verb

explanation.surface: A clog dance, performed in wooden shoes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clogs' looks like the shoes; it is a verb. BALLS loses its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A ball is a formal social gathering held for dancing.

clue.text: Shaving aid found in blazer Rod lost touring Austria

indicators.note: a tour goes round a place, so the letters go around the abbreviation
something lost has gone astray, so these letters are out of order

blocks.note: taken as written
A is the international vehicle code for Austria

explanation.surface: Rod finds a razor in the blazer he lost on holiday in Austria.
explanation.definitionFit: A razor blade is the sharp edge used in a razor to remove hair from the face.

clue.text: Old attempt to bury sad story

indicators.note: to bury something is to put it inside, so one word goes within the other

blocks.note: a try is an attempt
aged means old

explanation.surface: An old man's effort to bury a sad tale.
explanation.definitionFit: A tragedy is a drama or narrative with an unhappy, often fatal ending.

clue.text: Time to behave in all respects with diplomacy

blocks.note: T is the abbreviation for time
to act is to behave
fully means completely

explanation.surface: Advice that now is the moment to behave properly and diplomatically.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting tactfully means handling people with sensitivity so as not to cause offence, as a diplomat should.

clue.text: Managed to be sold around Louisiana as breakfast food

indicators.note: around means on every side, so one word encloses the other

blocks.note: at auction, an item about to be sold is going, going, gone
to run a business is to manage it
LA is the postal abbreviation for Louisiana

explanation.surface: A business managed to sell its goods across Louisiana as a breakfast cereal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going, going, gone' is the auctioneer's call, which is why to be sold can mean go.
explanation.definitionFit: Granola is a baked mixture of oats, nuts and honey eaten with milk in the morning.

clue.text: Begin harangue about hairpiece wife mislaid at home

indicators.note: something mislaid has gone missing, so that letter drops out
about means surrounding, so the speech word goes around the rest

blocks.note: to orate is to speechify at length
a wig is a hairpiece
W is the abbreviation for wife
someone at home is in

explanation.surface: A man starts ranting about the toupee his wife lost around the house.
explanation.definitionFit: To originate is to start or come into being, the intransitive sense of begin.

clue.text: Meeting shrink without resistance

indicators.note: without means lacking, so that letter is left out

blocks.note: to contract is to get smaller
R is the physics symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A session with a psychiatrist that goes smoothly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shrink' suggests a psychiatrist, but here it is a verb. CONTRACT loses its R.
explanation.definitionFit: Contact is coming together or touching, a coming into communication with someone.

clue.text: Out of sorts after count’s reprimand

blocks.note: to tell votes or money is to count it, as a bank teller does
feeling off is feeling unwell

explanation.surface: A nobleman, a count, is in a bad mood and scolds someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' puts OFF after TELL; the 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: To tell off is a phrasal verb meaning to scold someone for doing wrong.

clue.text: Recorded in history when Blues’ back moved up front and scored at the end

indicators.note: the rear letter is shifted to the start, a rotation of the word
at the end points to the final letter of the next word only

blocks.note: blue is the colour of Britain's Conservative Party, whose members are Tories
last letter of scored

explanation.surface: A football report: the Blues' defender pushed forward and scored late on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blues' and 'scored' suggest football; Blues here means Conservatives. TORIES with its S moved to the front is STORIE.
explanation.definitionFit: Storied means celebrated in stories or legend, so it is chronicled through the ages.

clue.text: Reproduction of a Rubens showing consumer of honey and insects

indicators.note: a reproduction is a remade copy, so the letters are rebuilt in another arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A print of a Rubens painting depicting an animal feeding.
explanation.definitionFit: The sun bear of Southeast Asia uses its long tongue to eat honey, termites and other insects.

clue.text: Not liable to run quickly

blocks.note: first meaning: of dyes, staying put in the wash
second meaning: at speed

explanation.surface: Someone too slow ever to be a runner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'run' suggests running away; the first meaning is about colours in fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Colourfast dye does not bleed in water, and the same word as an adverb means rapidly.

clue.text: Stern of extremely swift boat

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its two ends, so only the outside letters are kept

blocks.note: outer letters of swift
an ark is a boat, as in Noah's

explanation.surface: The back end of a very fast vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stern' looks like the rear of the boat; it is the adjective meaning severe.
explanation.definitionFit: Stark and stern both describe something severe, harsh or bleak in manner.

clue.text: Flashy head of Biology seen with Heather repeatedly

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, so only that one is kept

blocks.note: first letter of Biology
ling is the common heather plant
says to write the head letter and the plant a second time

explanation.surface: The showy head of the biology department is often seen with a colleague called Heather.
explanation.definitionFit: Bling-bling is slang for showy jewellery, and used as an adjective it means ostentatious.

clue.text: Large jar by the sound of it

indicators.note: going by how it sounds points to a word spoken alike but spelt differently

blocks.note: to grate is to jar, to sound harsh

explanation.surface: A big jar that rattles when shaken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jar' reads as a container but is the verb, to irritate.
explanation.definitionFit: Great is a plain synonym of big, of considerable size.

clue.text: So enthusiastic? Not entirely

indicators.note: not the entire word means only part of it is used, a run of letters inside

blocks.note: the letters run from the second to the fifth of enthusiastic

explanation.surface: A lukewarm reaction: so you are keen? Not really.
explanation.definitionFit: Thus and so both mean therefore, or in this way, as connective adverbs.

clue.text: Detestable mole angrily framing Athos in error

indicators.note: something done angrily is thrown about in a rage, so the letters are jumbled
a frame goes round a picture, so one set of letters encloses the other
in error means wrongly placed, so these letters too are out of order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A spy, a mole, furiously trapping Athos, one of the Three Musketeers, by mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: Both words are rearranged separately, each with its own signal, before one goes inside the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Loathsome describes something hateful that causes disgust, which is what detestable means.

clue.text: Make less from what a cricketer needs at end of game

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter, so only that one is kept

blocks.note: a batsman in cricket needs a bat
last letter of game

explanation.surface: A cricketer's kit list for the end of the match.
explanation.definitionFit: To abate something is to reduce its strength or amount, lessening it.

clue.text: Why mention president’s expression of alarm?

indicators.note: to mention a word is to say it, so what counts is how it is spoken

blocks.note: the letter Y is pronounced like the word why
Ike was the nickname of US President Dwight Eisenhower

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about why someone would bring up the president.
explanation.definitionFit: Yikes is an informal exclamation people use when startled or frightened.

clue.text: Pressure on me to find a piece of terrycloth good for stuffing

definitions.note: a noun phrase: a good, an item, used to stuff

indicators.note: a piece of a word here is just its opening letter

blocks.note: pressure is force applied
taken as written
taken as written
first letter of terrycloth

explanation.surface: Someone is pressured into finding a scrap of towelling that would make good padding.
explanation.definitionFit: Forcemeat is a seasoned mixture of chopped meat used to fill poultry or other dishes.
